SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) specifies a digital code format and modulation method to be used for timing and control purposes of television-tape audio separate machines and/or associated The encoded signal shall be recorded recorders. on the cue track or on an auxiliary longitudinal track. This standard is applicable for 50 HZ625 lines system. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, and definitions given in IS : 1885 1970* shall apply. 3. 3.1 The modulation method shall be such that a transition occurs at the beginning of every bit period. In the case of a `zero', there is no second transition within the bit period. In the a case of a `one', there is a second transition, half-bit period after the start of the bit. This method is also known as `Bi-Phase Mark' ( scc Fig. 1 ).

The bits shall be evenly spaced in such a way that the code word period shall coincide with the period of one television The bit rate shall be 80 times the frame frame. rate ( per second ) of the television system used. 4.6 Assigned and Unassigned Bits

1) 9 1988

4.5 Use of Binary Groups The binary groups are intended for the storage of supplementary data by the users. The 32 bits within the eight binary groups may be assigned in any way without restrictions, if the character set used for the data insertion is not specified and the binary group flag bits No. 27 and 43, both are zero. If an eight-bit character set conforming to IS : 10315-1982* and IS : l2326-1987t is signalled by the binary group flag bits No. 27 and 43, the characters should be inserted in accordance with Fig. 3. The information carried by the user bits is not subjected to any regulation. At present, Character the following set not specified truth-table applies: 0 1

4.6.1 Colour-Lock Flag Bit - The colour-lock flag bit No. I I shall be set to 1 when the time code is locked to the associated PAL colour signal in accordance with the eight-field sequence, and when the video signal has the `preferred subcarrier-to-line-sync phase'.

4.6.2 Bi-Phase Mark Phase-Correction Bit - The purpose of the phase-correction bit is to compensate for phase reversals in the bi-phase mark modulation that could occur when code inserts Such compensation may be are performed. required when code inserts modify the content of any of bits No. 0 to 63, bit No. 59 excluded. 4.6.2.1 In order that the magnetization transient between bit-cell 79 of one word and bit-cell 0 of the next shall always be in the same direction, bit No. 59 will be put in a state where every 80-bit word will contain an even number of logic zeros. 4.6.2.2 This requirement results following truth-table for bit No. 59: Number of Logic zeros in Bits NO. 0 to 63 ( 59 Excluded) Odd 1 0 in Bit 59 the

4.6.2.3 In drawing up this specification, the use of time code write/read systems that have equal polarity relations between input/output voltage and the tape magnetization is assumed. 4.6.2.4 This specification should not be understood as a requirement for time code insert capacity in television tape-machines in situations where tapes have to be interchanged, until further notice from the International Electrotechnical Commission ( IEC ). 4.6.3 Unassigned Bits - Bits No. 10 and 58 are reserved for future assignment and shall be zeros until specified by the International Electrotechnical Commission ( IEC ). 2

5. STRUCTURE OF THE TIME ADDRESS Recognition of these requirements can be accomplished with the aid of the time and control code, provided that there exists a fixed relationship between time address of the code and the sequence of television fields. This particular relationship is described below. 6.1.1 PAL Signals Systems B, G, H and IDuring electronic editing of colour signals recording on television tape-machines, itis important that in the case of sophisticated editing opeiations on PAL signals, the correct eight-field sequence also be maintained in the edited master, and that the `in-phase' or `out-of-phase' position of a slave tape can be controlled. These sequences can be preserved with the aid of the time-and-control code, provided that there exists a fixed relationship between the time addresses of the code and the sequence of television fields. Therefore, it has been agreed that, when necessary, the on-tape relationship between the time address-numbers of the time and control code and the associated eight fields of the PAL video signal, shall be as follows: bit No. 0 is A Hours Units Tens Bits 48-51: four 1, 2, 4, 8 count Bits 56-57: two 1, 2 count 0 to bits BCD 0 to 9. bits BCD 2. arranged arranged bit No. 16 is B bit No. 8 is C bit No. 8 is D bit No. 17 is E bit No. 24 is F the time-code is displayed in decimal When S and P designating the numbers of numbers, ~~~ 1. and ^ seconas pictures respectively, the above condition is expressed as: remainder on dividing S + P by 4 is

5.1 The basic structure of the time address is based upon the Binary Coded Decimal ( BCD ) system. In those cases, when the count does not rise to 9, only two or three bits are required, rather than four bits as is normal in the BCD code. 5.2 Assignment Frames Units Tens Seconds Units Tens Minutes Units Tens Bits 32-35: four bits BCD arranged 1,2,4,8countOto9. 6. ADDITIONAL COLOUR REQUIREMENTS

6.1 Field Sequence of Colour Recordings - Simple editing of colour signals on television timing disturtape machines where a picture of the colour bance of up to half the period subcarrier can be tolerated need only consider a four field sequency in PAL. Sophisticated editing operations, where disturbance must be held to a minimum, shall take into account an eight-field PAL sequence. The phase relationship between colour subcarrier and the synchronizing signal should show minimum discontinuity at the edit point.

0 for fields 7 and 8 1 for fields 1 and 2 2 for fields 3 and 4 3 for fields 5 and 6 6.2 The' requirements of 6.1 shall be met at the output of the time and control code generator.
